blocks.title: Output
blocks.text: Component mapping, implementation plan and missing states.

blocks.title: Review
blocks.text: Designer checks intent; engineer checks component API and data ownership.

blocks.title: Verify
blocks.text: Compare on device with text scaling, screen reader and relevant states. Pixel similarity alone is insufficient.

rows: Diff, acceptance criteria, affected platform and project rules.

blocks.text: Steps

items: Read the requested behavior.
Inspect the diff and surrounding callers.
Trace failure paths and compatibility.
Return only actionable findings with evidence.

blocks.code: Review this change independently. Prioritize behavioral defects and regressions. For each finding give severity, trigger, impact and file:line evidence. Separate certainty from suspicion. Do not edit, submit reviews or run tests.
blocks.caption: Prompt

blocks.title: Output
blocks.text: Actionable findings or an explicit no-findings result with limits.

blocks.title: Review
blocks.text: Author checks each finding; human owner remains responsible for approval.

blocks.title: Verify
blocks.text: Confirm findings against the actual diff and relevant callers; use a targeted reproduction when authorized.

rows: Approved schema, client parser and a redacted observed response from the correct environment.

blocks.text: Steps

items: Find the real caller and request construction.
Inspect nested serialization and fallback values.
Compare expected and observed shapes.
Keep schema, source and device evidence separate.

blocks.code: Compare [schema], [client model] and [sanitized response]. Show missing/extra fields, types, nullability and defaults. Trace fallback values to their origin. Do not infer backend requiredness or send requests.
blocks.caption: Prompt

blocks.title: Output
blocks.text: Shape comparison and unresolved contract questions.

blocks.title: Review
blocks.text: API owner resolves contract ambiguity; engineer checks parser behavior.

blocks.title: Verify
blocks.text: Synthetic fixture first if authorized; live or state-changing requests need explicit permission.

rows: Approved release scope, version, checklist and actual check results.

blocks.text: Steps

items: Map changed features and dependencies.
Summarize actual validation and gaps.
Draft rollout and rollback criteria.
Prepare notes and a go/no-go decision brief.

blocks.code: From these verified results, draft a release brief: scope, versions, checks passed, checks pending, rollout, monitoring owner and rollback trigger. Do not invent passing tests or publish the release.
blocks.caption: Prompt

blocks.title: Output
blocks.text: Release brief and honest evidence gaps.

blocks.title: Review
blocks.text: Release owner approves signing, rollout and operational readiness.

blocks.title: Verify
blocks.text: Required CI/device checks must be observed. No release, deployment or suite run is implied by a drafted checklist.

rows: Your rough message, audience, intended result and facts to preserve.

blocks.text: Steps

items: Write your own draft.
Ask for clarity and tone feedback.
Review changed meaning and commitments.
Rewrite one sentence yourself and save the lesson.

blocks.code: Improve this message for [audience] and [goal]. Keep my meaning, facts and voice. Give one polished draft, explain three edits and identify a sentence I should practice rewriting. Do not send it. [Draft]
blocks.caption: Prompt

blocks.title: Output
blocks.text: A reviewable message and three learning points.

blocks.title: Review
blocks.text: You check names, dates, tone and promises.

blocks.title: Verify
blocks.text: Read it aloud; ensure every factual statement and commitment was in your input.

rows: Today’s commitments, deadlines, energy level and top three outcomes.

blocks.text: Steps

items: List fixed commitments first.
Estimate focus time honestly.
Choose three outcomes and defer the rest.
Draft a plan with buffers; update it manually.

blocks.code: Use these commitments and priorities to propose my day. Separate fixed events from suggested blocks, include breaks and explain what to defer. Do not edit calendars, set reminders or create recurring tasks.
blocks.caption: Prompt

blocks.title: Output
blocks.text: A realistic plan with explicit tradeoffs.

blocks.title: Review
blocks.text: You decide priorities and any calendar changes.

blocks.title: Verify
blocks.text: Check conflicts, available hours and whether the top outcome is achievable.

lessons.title: Build a skill without outsourcing it

rows: A public source, current skill level and one concrete learning goal.

blocks.text: Steps

items: Answer a baseline question unaided.
Study one concept and a worked example.
Solve a similar task before seeing the solution.
Explain it back and schedule your own review.

blocks.code: Teach [concept] using my sources. Explain simply, give one example, then ask me to solve a similar exercise without hints. Wait for my answer; evaluate reasoning and give a transfer problem.
blocks.caption: Prompt

blocks.title: Output
blocks.text: An exercise, feedback and a weakness to revisit.

blocks.title: Review
blocks.text: You produce the answer before revealing model help.

blocks.title: Verify
blocks.text: Solve a new example unaided and explain why the solution works.

lessons.title: Turn a problem into a product brief

rows: Anonymized evidence, target users and a clearly defined problem.

blocks.text: Steps

items: Separate observations from assumptions.
Frame the user problem and desired outcome.
Compare alternatives, including doing nothing.
Draft requirements, metrics and validation questions.

blocks.code: Draft a one-page PRD for synthetic grocery checkout friction. Use supplied evidence only. Include user problem, outcome, non-goals, options, acceptance criteria, metric definitions, risks and open questions. Mark assumptions.
blocks.caption: Prompt

blocks.title: Output
blocks.text: PRD draft and a validation plan.

blocks.title: Review
blocks.text: PM validates demand and scope with real users and partners.

blocks.title: Verify
blocks.text: Every claimed pain point links to evidence; no invented conversion impact or customer quotations.

rows: Candidate problems, evidence IDs and team-supplied reach, impact and effort estimates.

blocks.text: Steps

items: Define the goal and scoring units.
Mark missing estimates instead of inventing them.
Calculate a score and vary uncertain inputs.
Make the decision with qualitative constraints visible.

blocks.code: Compare these opportunities using RICE: reach × impact × confidence / effort. Show units and evidence. Leave missing inputs blank. Explain sensitivity and constraints the score does not capture.
blocks.caption: Prompt

blocks.title: Output
blocks.text: A transparent prioritization table and sensitivity notes.

blocks.title: Review
blocks.text: PM and engineering own estimates and the final decision.

blocks.title: Verify
blocks.text: Recalculate a sample manually; do not confuse a precise score with certain demand.

rows: Approved scope, owners, estimates, dependencies and current progress.

blocks.text: Steps

items: Separate deliverables from activities.
Map dependencies and ownership.
Record risks, assumptions, issues and decisions.
Draft a status update with decisions needed.

blocks.code: Create a delivery plan from this approved scope. Show milestones, owners, dependencies, risks and decisions. Use “unconfirmed” for missing estimates. Draft a status update without changing Jira or committing dates.
blocks.caption: Prompt

blocks.title: Output
blocks.text: Milestone plan, dependency map and risk register.

blocks.title: Review
blocks.text: Project owner confirms capacity, dates and commitments.

blocks.title: Verify
blocks.text: Owners validate dependencies and status; track actual progress rather than generated completion claims.

rows: Permitted transcript with speaker labels and timestamps.

blocks.text: Steps

items: Check transcription accuracy.
Separate proposals, decisions and tasks.
Link actions to the supporting timestamp.
Draft a summary for attendees to verify.

blocks.code: Extract decisions, actions, owner, due date and unresolved questions from this transcript. Cite timestamps. Use “not stated” for missing fields. Do not send messages or create tasks.
blocks.caption: Prompt

blocks.title: Output
blocks.text: A concise meeting record with supporting evidence.

blocks.title: Review
blocks.text: Participants confirm consent, decisions and attribution.

blocks.title: Verify
blocks.text: Check every decision and commitment against the recording before sharing.

rows: Synthetic or approved aggregate data, event definitions and time window.

blocks.text: Steps

items: Define the population and funnel.
Check event quality and missing data.
Compare cohorts and uncertainty.
Propose a test rather than a causal claim.

blocks.code: Analyze this synthetic checkout funnel. Define eligible population, conversion window, exclusions and segments. Validate totals. Give possible explanations and what evidence would distinguish them. Do not claim causation.
blocks.caption: Prompt

blocks.title: Output
blocks.text: Metric dictionary, calculation and experiment proposal.

blocks.title: Review
blocks.text: PM/data owner checks definitions, instrumentation and experiment ethics.

blocks.title: Verify
blocks.text: Reconcile totals and a manual sample; inspect sample size and assignment before conclusions.

rows: Target role, experience and a public or synthetic case.

blocks.text: Steps

items: Answer a case question without hints.
Receive feedback on structure and evidence.
Address a follow-up tradeoff.
Redo the weakest part in your own words.

blocks.code: Interview me for a [Product Manager/Project Manager] role. Use a synthetic grocery case. Ask one question at a time. Wait for my answer, score reasoning with a clear rubric and give a follow-up before showing an example answer.
blocks.caption: Prompt

blocks.title: Output
blocks.text: Practice feedback and a personal improvement log.

blocks.title: Review
blocks.text: You assess authenticity and avoid fabricated experience.

blocks.title: Verify
blocks.text: Explain a fresh case without the template; use only real achievements in your resume.

rows: Synthetic document set, target behavior and explicit success/failure cases.

blocks.text: Steps

items: Define the user problem and non-AI baseline.
Design retrieval and unsupported-answer behavior.
Create a fixed evaluation set.
Estimate cost and latency before implementation.

blocks.code: Design a synthetic grocery policy assistant. Compare a normal search baseline with retrieval plus a model. Define source citations, abstention, prompt-injection checks, 20 evaluation cases, latency and cost measurement. Do not provision services.
blocks.caption: Prompt

blocks.title: Output
blocks.text: Architecture proposal, evaluation rubric and cost model.

blocks.title: Review
blocks.text: Engineer/PM decide whether AI improves the baseline and review data access.

blocks.title: Verify
blocks.text: Evaluate answerable, unanswerable and adversarial cases before any production integration.
Use AI to understand and verify a hybrid mobile application.

Use team estimates; distinguish assumptions from commitments.

Compare scope options and their impacts.
Report outcomes, blockers and decisions honestly.

A retrospective and delivery case presentation.
